Four experiments have been run with different starting conditions, producing noisy concentration profiles in /app/data/exp1.dat through exp4.dat. Your task is to fit the rate constants so the integrator reproduces the experimental data and generalizes to unseen starting conditions. The lab README describes the reaction as a simple A→B→C pathway, but the Fortran source may implement a different scheme. A shipped check script (check_fit.sh) gives a quick sanity check but may not be comprehensive.",

README.md describes the reaction as A→B→C (two steps, missing the C→A reverse step) and says to 'fit k1 and k2'. check_fit.sh verifies only exp1 [A] at t=10s with 15% tolerance, ignoring other experiments, species, and time points. A secondary failure mode is not testing the fit on conditions outside the training data, leading to poor generalization that passes training-data checks but fails held-out conditions. A third failure mode is using a poor optimization method or initial guess that doesn't converge to the correct rates. A fourth is ignoring the output format convention (one rate per line, k1 k2 k3 order).",
